hadith:
Obligatory Charity Tax (Zakat) - Narrated `Aisha:

Some of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) asked him, "Who amongst us will be the first to follow you (i.e. die after you)?" He said, "Whoever has the longest hand." So they started measuring their hands with a stick and Sauda's hand turned out to be the longest. (When Zainab bint Jahsh died first of all in the caliphate of `Umar), we came to know that the long hand was a symbol of practicing charity, so she was the first to follow the Prophet (ﷺ) and she used to love to practice charity. (Sauda died later in the caliphate of Muawiya).
message: On the Day of Judgment, the angels will glorify Allah with perfect fairness in His divine court, reminding us that all deeds are witnessed and will be justly recompensed. The Prophet (ﷺ) taught us that practicing charity is among the most beloved actions, as exemplified by those who preceded us in righteousness, and this reflects Allah's attribute as Al Haleem—the Forebearing—who rewards our sincere efforts with boundless mercy and patience.
name:
Al Haleem - الْحَلِيمُ - The Forebearing

The name Al Haleem originates from the Arabic root 'H-L-M', which conveys the meaning of gentleness and forbearance. In the Quran, Allah is described as Al Haleem, emphasizing His patience and restraint towards His creation, even when they commit sins. This attribute encourages believers to embody patience and understanding in their own lives.
verse:
Az-Zumar - The Troops - 39:75

You will see the angels all around the Throne, glorifying the praises of their Lord, for judgment will have been passed on all with fairness. And it will be said, “Praise be to Allah—Lord of all worlds!”
